Paragraph:
Translation: In the presence of Bhisma, Drona and all other chieftains of the world, Hrsikesa, the Lord, said, Just behold, Partha, all the Kurus who are assembled here.

Purport: As the Supersoul of all living entities, Lord Krsna could understand what was going on in the mind of Arjuna. The use of the word Hrsikesa in this connection indicates that He knew everything... Now what did Krsna mean when He told Arjuna to 'behold the Kurus'? Did Arjuna want to stop there and not fight? Krsna never expected such things from the son of His aunt Prtha. The mind of Arjuna was thus predicated by the Lord in friendly joking.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Having positioned the chariot, Krishna speaks to Arjuna. He specifically draws Arjuna's attention to the presence of his most revered elders (Bhisma and Drona) and tells him to 'behold' his family members.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna acts as a catalyst. Knowing exactly what is in Arjuna's subconscious mind, Krishna intentionally forces Arjuna to look at his beloved relatives, pushing him towards the emotional confrontation he must face.
Outcome/Resolution: By instructing Arjuna to look at his loved ones arrayed as enemies, Krishna triggers the massive psychological collapse and emotional outpouring that will form the basis of the entire Bhagavad Gita.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Antaryami (The inner witness or Supersoul who knows the deepest thoughts of the mind)
Moha (The impending illusion of bodily attachment that Krishna is about to expose)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna, acting as the omniscient Supersoul, sets the divine play in motion. He deliberately forces Arjuna to face his strongest material attachments (his grandfather and teacher). This gentle, seemingly innocuous instruction ('behold the Kurus') is designed to crack open Arjuna's material ego so that spiritual wisdom can be poured in.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is the precise moment of 'flooding' or direct confrontation in a therapeutic sense. Krishna acts as an incisive guide, pushing Arjuna to confront the most painful aspect of his reality: fighting those he deeply loves. Krishna intentionally triggers Arjuna's latent cognitive dissonance to bring the underlying psychological conflict to the surface where it can be treated.
